summary: This section of a statistics course reviews sampling distributions of the sample mean and introduces bootstrapping, a resampling method for approximating the sampling distribution of a statistic when the underlying distribution is unknown. Bootstrapping resamples with replacement from a single sample to estimate standard errors and build confidence intervals, for example for the median. The note also includes R code for simulating a sampling distribution and bootstrapping a median.
one_line: An introduction to bootstrapping, a resampling method that estimates sampling distributions and confidence intervals from a single sample.
key_facts: If the population is Normal or the sample size is large (rule of thumb n>30), the sampling distribution of the sample mean is approximately Normal.
The sampling distribution of the sample mean has standard deviation σ/√n and estimated standard error s/√n.
Bootstrapping is a resampling procedure that uses data from one sample to generate a sampling distribution by repeatedly sampling with replacement from that sample.

The bootstrap steps for the median are: replace the population with the sample, sample with replacement B times, compute each sample median M_i, and obtain the approximate distribution of the sample median.
The note recommends B to be large, say 1000.
The standard error of the sample median can be estimated by the standard deviation of M_1,...,M_B.
Sampling with replacement is essential, because without it every bootstrap sample median would equal the observed sample median.
For a 90% confidence interval, the 5th and 95th percentiles of the bootstrap sample are used.
The same bootstrap steps apply to any statistic; only the calculated statistic changes from the median to another statistic.
The note mentions parametric, nonparametric, and weighted bootstraps as variants, but only introduces the basics.
The bootstrap.median R function takes a data vector, B = 1000 and confidence = 0.95 as defaults, and reports the percentiles and median of the bootstrap medians.
The sampling.distribution R function simulates normal data with defaults n = 100, B = 1000, mean = 5, sd = 1 and confidence = 0.95 to approximate the sampling distribution of the median.
